texts: Mixed intensity laps - half easy, half moderate.

The goal of this workout is to improve the forearm's ability to work aerobically on easy terrain and recover from harder climbing whilst still on the wall.

Find an easy route or circuit of 30 moves or more which shares the same section of wall as a harder climb of a similar length.
  
Part 1: Climb the first half of the easy route which is 15 moves long. This route must be far easier than your on-sight limit grade.
Part 2: At 15 moves switch to the harder climb and continue for a further 15 moves until 30 moves are completed in total. This harder section should be around your on-sight grade.
By finishing parts 1 and 2 you should have climbed one route or circuit and therefore completed rep 1. 

Complete 4 reps with as little rest as possible between each climb. If you are on a rope you can be lowered to the start quickly between reps. If using a circuit board, aim to continue climbing non stop for all 4 reps. 
 
During the easier section of climbing, try to recover as much as possible in order to feel fresh before the harder section of climbing. Rest 10 minutes between sets, completing 3 sets total.

What to record? When logging this session please choose a grade which is half way between the difficulty of the two chosen sections of climbing. 
e.g. 5:10 + 5:12 = 5:11 logged for this session.

If climbing on a rope using routes which are shorter than 30 moves in length, complete the first 15 moves on an easier climb, lower to the ground and immediately climb the next 15 moves on a separate harder route. This will mean each set will include 8 climbs up rather than 4.
